Guides.Title: Guides
Guides.EmptyTitle: Choose a game to see its guides
Guides.EmptyMessage: Choose a game from the sidebar selector. Shared guides and tips for that game will appear here.
Guides.EmptyList: There are no guides for this game yet.
Guides.General.ProfilePackage.Title: Profiles and modpacks: what is the difference?
Guides.General.ProfilePackage.Summary: A modpack describes a shareable set; a profile prepares it locally for launch.
Guides.General.ProfilePackage.Step1: A modpack contains the set's contents: mods, pinned versions, sources, and required dependencies. It can be shared with other players.
Guides.General.ProfilePackage.Step2: A profile is a local configuration for a particular game. It stores the selected contents and launch settings—it does not alter the game installation itself.
Guides.General.ProfilePackage.Step3: Use separate profiles for testing or different sets. Review the plan and compatibility before applying changes, and agree on the same pinned versions with your group before playing together.
Guides.General.Compatibility.Title: How compatibility works
Guides.General.Compatibility.Summary: Compatibility depends on the game, its build, and the complete mod set—not just a mod's name.
Guides.General.Compatibility.Step1: Check the detected game version, distribution (for example, Steam), architecture, and mod loader. These details can change which file is required.
Guides.General.Compatibility.Step2: Compare the requirements of pinned mod versions and their dependencies. Game, mod-loader, and modpack compatibility are separate questions.
Guides.General.Compatibility.Step3: If compatibility is unconfirmed or the plan reports a conflict, do not force the install. Choose a compatible version or wait for a verified release.
Guides.Valheim.FirstSetup.Title: First Valheim setup: Steam and Proton
Guides.Valheim.FirstSetup.Summary: Prepare a separate profile, check requirements, and review the change plan first.
Guides.Valheim.FirstSetup.Step1: In Library, select the correct Steam Valheim installation and check its detected game version. On Linux, decide whether you are using the native build or the Windows build through Proton.
Guides.Valheim.FirstSetup.Step2: If you use Proton, enable it for this game in Steam's compatibility settings and launch through the same installation and prefix. Do not mix files from another prefix.
Guides.Valheim.FirstSetup.Step3: Create a separate Valheim profile and add mods with their required dependencies. Choose files intended for the selected operating system and mod loader.
Guides.Valheim.FirstSetup.Step4: Review the plan before applying changes. Once the profile is prepared, launch the game with it; if something goes wrong, switch back to a clean profile and check the compatibility report.
Guides.AmongUs.TownOfUs.Title: Choosing a Town of Us Mira release
Guides.AmongUs.TownOfUs.Summary: Match the mod file to the Among Us distribution and architecture; labels alone do not prove compatibility.
Guides.AmongUs.TownOfUs.Step1: Check which Among Us distribution and installation you use, along with the game's architecture. Do not assume a Steam release also works with the itch build.
Guides.AmongUs.TownOfUs.Step2: Selection hint: according to the PAK-59 notes from September 2026, the Town of Us Mira release for Steam is x64, while the itch release is x32. This is a hint, not a guarantee that every file is compatible.
Guides.AmongUs.TownOfUs.Step3: Open the release specified by the author and check its description, requirements, and exact file name. Confirm the game version and required mod loader before pinning the file to a separate profile.
Guides.AmongUs.TownOfUs.Step4: Review the plan and compatibility message. If the architecture, game build, or mod requirements do not match, do not force the install—find the correct variant or wait for confirmation from the author.
Guides.AmongUs.CleanGame.Title: Return to a clean Among Us game
Guides.AmongUs.CleanGame.Summary: Launch the game without mods while keeping your existing profile for later.
Guides.AmongUs.CleanGame.Step1: Before launch, open the profile selector and choose the clean (mod-free) profile, not your modified Among Us profile.
Guides.AmongUs.CleanGame.Step2: Launch the game with that profile. If you do not see a clean profile, create a separate empty profile instead of deleting or overwriting the existing one.
Guides.AmongUs.CleanGame.Step3: To use mods again, select the saved profile. Switching the active profile should not remove its contents or pinned versions.
HelpTip.Profile.Label: Profile
HelpTip.Profile.Content: A profile is a local game configuration with a selected mod set and launch settings. A modpack describes a set that can be shared; a profile lets you use it separately with this installation.
HelpTip.Compatibility.Label: Compatibility
HelpTip.Compatibility.Content: Checks consider the game build, distribution, architecture, mod loader, and requirements of pinned mod versions. An unverified result does not mean a set will definitely work.
HelpTip.GitHubRelease.Label: GitHub release
HelpTip.GitHubRelease.Content: Choose the repository and exact release specified by the author. Check its tag, requirements, and correct file; the latest release or a beta file may not match your game.
HelpTip.RecipeStudio.Label: Recipe Studio
HelpTip.RecipeStudio.Content: Recipe Studio helps prepare a modpack recipe. Check the game version, file sources, dependencies, and plan preview before applying changes.
